findings.description: Nudge pot pays the FULL nudgePaymentToken balance to a caller-chosen `recipient` on a count-only gate (`count >= nudgeSize`), decoupled from the value the caller contributed. A permissionless actor who mints >= nudgeSize real mints first sweeps the entire externally-funded USDC pot. The `minReward` slippage floor added in this version only stops the LOSER from paying mint costs for a sniped reward (self-protection); it explicitly does NOT stop the front-run of the pot (see NatSpec lines 224-229). This is the KNOWN H-01/M-01 lineage (story-014 pinned the minter to close the fake-mint drain; the MEV front-run of a legitimately-funded pot + owner over-funding footgun survive per ledger).
presentMitigations: pot snapshotted BEFORE the mint loop (line 271-275) -> donate-forward, no same-tx self-refund (satisfies notVulnerableWhen 'pot snapshotted BEFORE the loop')
minter pinned to owner-set state (story-014) -> qualifying requires paying for >= nudgeSize real mints
minReward floor rolls back the whole batch if deliverable reward < floor
missingMitigations: payout still not bounded by the caller's own contributed value (vulnerableWhen) — whoever clears the count gate first takes the entire balance-based pot
findings.ledgerNote: Reconcile against BatchNFTMinter nudge ledger entries (H-01 fixed story-014; MEV front-run + over-funding footgun previously accepted). Surfaced for sanitizer adjudication — do NOT auto-suppress; confirm the current minReward addition did not change the accepted boundary.

findings.description: emergencyWithdraw decrements `totalStaked` (line 545) but does NOT call `_recomputeSchedule` — unlike `stake`/`unstake` which both re-size the rate against the new pool via a tail recompute (lines 455, 476). In the APY model `rewardRate = S * targetAPY / SECONDS_PER_YEAR` with `S = totalStaked * latestPrice`, so after an emergency exit the rate stays sized for the OLD (larger) pool while `_updatePool` divides `elapsed * rewardRate` by the now-smaller `totalStaked`, over-emitting to the surviving stakers (bounded by rewardBudget) until the next stake/unstake/claim recompute. This is the known M-02 class.
presentMitigations: any subsequent stake/unstake/claim triggers a recompute that re-sizes the rate
over-emission is bounded by rewardBudget (cannot exceed funded budget) and _safePay reverts on true shortfall
missingMitigations: no recompute at the point totalStaked changes in emergencyWithdraw (accrual settled at OLD rate against NEW smaller pool between exit and next interaction)
findings.ledgerNote: This is M-02 (run-16), owner-acknowledged WON'T-FIX (deployed + no migrate-on-behalf, pullAndRefresh mitigation). Surfaced explicitly per regression policy; sanitizer/ledger reconciles to won't-fix.

findings.description: Same M-02 class as PM-19-002, present in the HAND-MAINTAINED PriceScaled copy: emergencyWithdraw (line 577) reduces `totalStaked` (line 584) without a tail `_recomputeSchedule`, while stake/unstake carry the tail recompute (lines 494, 515). PriceScaled uses the identical APY rate model (`S = totalStaked * latestPrice * priceScale`), so the stale-rate over-emission window is identical. Flagged separately because the two files are maintained independently (fork-drift watch): a fix to NFTStaker.emergencyWithdraw would NOT auto-propagate here.
presentMitigations: bounded by rewardBudget; _safePay reverts on shortfall
missingMitigations: no recompute at the totalStaked mutation in emergencyWithdraw
findings.ledgerNote: Same root cause as M-02; PriceScaled is the story-017 clone. Reconcile with M-02 won't-fix but confirm the copy is covered by the same acknowledgement (memory watch-note: NFTStaker fixes must be manually mirrored to PriceScaled + Depletion).

findings.description: batchMint has NO ReentrancyGuard/nonReentrant (BatchNFTMinter does not inherit ReentrancyGuard) yet its mint loop calls `nftMinter.mint(_dispatcherIndex, recipient)` (line 281), which mints an ERC1155 to a caller-controlled `recipient` and therefore invokes `onERC1155Received` on that recipient MID-LOOP, before the nudge pot is paid (line 295) and before the dust refund (line 299-305). This is the classic inbound-receive-hook reentrancy surface the pattern codifies. The nudge pot is snapshotted BEFORE the loop, and any reentrant batchMint would (a) re-read the snapshot, and (b) execute `forceApprove(nftMinter, 0)` which zeroes the allowance the outer loop still depends on, causing the outer mint to revert — so the current mitigations appear to make reentry self-defeating (revert, no drain). Flagged as a pattern match (confidence that the surface exists is high; confidence that it is EXPLOITABLE is medium/low) — recall over tidiness: manual verification of the nested-approval / nested-pot interaction is warranted before dismissing.
matchedSignatures: nftMinter.mint(_dispatcherIndex, recipient) [line 281 — ERC1155 mint to caller-controlled recipient]
nudge pot transfer + dust refund AFTER the mint loop (state/value moves post-hook)
presentMitigations: nudge pot snapshotted BEFORE the loop (line 271-275)
nested forceApprove(nftMinter,0) breaks the outer loop's max allowance -> outer mint reverts on reentry
final safeTransfer of the pot reverts if balance insufficient (a nested payout would drain balance and revert the outer transfer)
missingMitigations: no explicit reentrancy guard — safety relies entirely on the snapshot-before-loop + allowance-revert emergent behaviour, which is fragile to future edits (e.g. moving the approval or making it per-call)
findings.ledgerNote: Confirm against prior BatchNFTMinter reviews (H-01 story-014 concerned the caller-supplied minter, a different vector). Recommend adding nonReentrant defensively even if currently non-exploitable.

manualReview.description: Immutable `priceScale` multiplies `latestPrice` (line 435) with no upper bound beyond the constructor `!= 0` guard. A deployer who sets the wrong magnitude (e.g. 1e12 vs 1 for an 18dp dispatcher, or 1e18) swings the emission rate / notional by orders of magnitude, and `totalStaked * latestPrice` overflow is only argued safe for `priceScale <= 1e12` (NatSpec lines 407-411). Non-obvious owner footgun (Law 3 operational hazard). This is the known L-08.
manualReview.ledgerNote: Matches L-08 (run-17). Route to triage; do not re-escalate above Low.

manualReview.description: unstake performs the outbound ERC1155 `safeTransferFrom(this -> msg.sender)` (line 471 / PriceScaled 510) — invoking `onERC1155Received` on a caller-controlled recipient — BEFORE the tail `_recomputeSchedule` (line 476 / 515). During that callback `totalStaked` is already decremented but `rewardRate`/`windowEnd` still reflect the old pool, so value-reporting views (`pendingReward`, `currentRewardRate`, `totalDebt`, `runwaySeconds`) return a transiently inconsistent snapshot. State-changing reentry is blocked by `nonReentrant`; impact requires an external integrator that prices off these views mid-callback — none is known. Surfaced for completeness (Law 1: the victim of read-only reentrancy is the downstream integrator, not this contract).
manualReview.ledgerNote: No known downstream consumer of these views as an oracle. Low/likely-informational; confirm no integrator reads staker views for collateral valuation.

manualReview.description: DISPATCHER_INDEX is hardcoded ASSUMED = 4 (line 48, NatSpec admits the operator must confirm against the live minter) and USDC is hardcoded as the nudge token. The broadcast guards check `USDC != TOKEN_MINTER` and `nudgeSize != 0` but do NOT verify on-chain that the nudge token (USDC) differs from the pinned dispatcher's `primeToken()` — that invariant is only enforced at batchMint runtime (revert), not at deploy. A wrong DISPATCHER_INDEX pins the batcher to the wrong dispatcher / payment asset. Non-obvious operator footgun; the script mitigates by documenting the required manual confirmation and by the runtime guard.
manualReview.ledgerNote: Operational/deploy hazard, not a contract bug. Route to QA/triage.

manualReview.description: story-020 (@321d0a9) correctly removed the bare stake/unstake tail recomputes and gated `_syncBudget` recompute on `inflow > 0`, closing the M-01 rate-drift in user paths (verified against the fix diff). However `depositFor` (migrator-only, Active-only) RETAINS an unconditional tail `_recomputeSchedule` (line 767) which resets `windowEnd = now + windowSeconds` and re-derives `rate = budget/windowSeconds` on every call. This is NOT the M-01 exploit class (not user-triggerable, not a bare interaction) — it is the intended post-migration window restart — but it is the one surviving unconditional recompute in a non-mint path and is called this cleanly. Flagged as a fork-drift / completeness watch-note, not a live finding.
manualReview.ledgerNote: M-01 fix confirmed faithful in user paths. depositFor recompute is intended migration semantics; confirm it is not repeatably invocable to grief the window.

patternsSkipped.reason: note: C4 treats as QA/known-issue. No user-facing approve(non-zero,non-zero) race; BatchNFTMinter uses internal forceApprove(max)->forceApprove(0) around its own mint loop. No HM twist. Skipped as primary finding per SKIP RULE.
